A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same JustAsk study and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–M. Sections and displays can be matched across renumbering, and the appendices retain their substantive content.

before.justification: v1 reports original Claude Code extraction results, experiments on 41 black-box models, controlled defense evaluations, and extraction and identity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, component ablations, repeated-seed agent evaluations, and production-system extraction results in Tables 5–8.

M1.justification: The core UCB procedure, default skill taxonomy, and Appendix B algorithm remain unchanged. v2 introduces an evaluated +Raccoon variant that adds Raccoon templates to the selectable skill pool (Section 4.8, Table 8), implementing an extension contemplated in v1. The fixed-taxonomy explanation in Section 3.1 clarifies the existing learner.

E1.justification: Section 4.8 substantially extends deployment coverage beyond the original Claude Code case with evaluations on Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, Cursor Agent CLI, Perplexity Sonar, and Copilot CLI. These add native assistant environments and prompt configurations, including two systems with source-accessible reference prompts. Original coverage remains.

E2.justification: v2 directly evaluates PLeak, Raccoon, and Zhang et al.'s output-inversion method in Tables 5 and 8; v1 discussed these works without such comparisons. Tables 6–7 also introduce bare-agent, introspection-only, random-selection, and unguided controls. The original defense comparators remain.

E3.justification: New protocols include a four-model comparison using a known 1,168-token prompt and best ground-truth similarity at B=3, Sonnet 4 ablations at B=3/5/10, six-model agent evaluation at B=5, and production evaluation with UCB at B=15. These supplement the unchanged original B=20 setup rather than establish reruns under its conditions.

E4.justification: Tables 6–7 add substantive tests of skill selection, UCB, query budget, and full versus unguided agents. These directly examine the framework's contribution beyond simple requests and random exploration. Existing defense and threshold analyses remain, but v1's detailed convergence table is removed while its aggregate finding is retained.

E5.justification: Table 7 newly reports means and standard deviations over three seeds for the six-model agent comparison. v1 had no comparable across-seed uncertainty reporting. The existing convergence correlation and p-value remain unchanged; the new reporting does not establish increased replication of the original experiments.

E6.justification: Tables 5–8 add extensive results: for example, GPT-4o at B=3 scores 0.727 for JustAsk versus 0.701 for Raccoon, and production-system averages are 0.703 versus 0.606. The full agent outperforms the unguided agent on five of six targets but scores lower on Mistral Large. Original black-box and defense scores remain unchanged. v1 Table 7's per-turn convergence values disappear, although r=0.94 remains reported.

T1.justification: The UCB equation and update rule, Appendix B algorithm, and Appendix C similarity definitions remain unchanged. No new theorem, proof, substantive mathematical derivation, or formal assumption is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same framework, 41-model extraction claim, HHH and identity findings, and 18.4% defense reduction. The added conclusion paragraph about downstream attacks reiterates risks already raised in v1's introduction and discussion rather than introducing a new central capability claim.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly defines self-evolution as selection-policy adaptation over fixed, hand-designed skills and interprets the new ablations as evidence for adaptive selection. Its limitations now distinguish black-box consistency from accuracy and explain paraphrase-bounded fidelity. These are substantive qualifications within otherwise largely retained interpretations.

D1.justification: A new footnote announces a project repository containing code, data, and extracted ground-truth files; v1 lacks this project-access information. v2 also documents the new comparison prompt's length and source-prompt validation for two CLIs. The PDFs establish these disclosures, not the linked resources' accessibility.

R1.justification: v2 adds Ma et al. (2025) on model and agent safety and Wu et al. (2026) on internal safety collapse. It further positions adaptive selection against fixed extraction strategies and describes incorporating prior templates. Changed author lists for PANDORA, RACE, ProxyPrompt, and other retained works are bibliographic updates rather than new cited research.

P1.justification: The related-work prose is condensed, and the method explanation, conclusion, and limitations receive localized revisions. Three experimental subsections and acknowledgements are added, alongside correspondence and bibliographic edits. Most existing prose and the appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The empirical displays are substantially expanded with baseline, budget-ablation, uncertainty, and production-comparison tables (v2 Tables 5–8). v1's HHH summary and convergence tables are removed; the HHH values remain in prose. Figure 5 moves later, while the existing figures and overall visual style are preserved.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked direct evidence establishing the framework's value over simpler agents and prior extraction methods. v2's controlled comparisons, component and budget ablations, and repeated-seed evaluation address that central deficiency and expose conditions where the framework helps or fails. Clearer fidelity limitations also improve interpretation. Removing the convergence table reduces transparency, and reference prompts for the closed production systems remain underexplained, but the added controlled evidence substantially improves the paper overall.
